metadata.generator: text-to-robot design engine (real components + printed structure)
notes: Interpreted locally: type inferred, DOF=3, gripper=parallel.

design.summary: Parallel gripper: 60 mm stroke, 47 N rated squeeze per finger, Feetech STS3215 C047 12 V 30 kg.cm (1:345)

joints.note: servo torque on the pinion; squeeze force per finger = torque / (2 x 10.5 mm pitch radius). finger_a is the actuated prismatic joint; finger_b and the pinion mimic it

checks.name: grip:fingers_parallel
checks.detail: rack-and-pinion (m1.5, 14 teeth, pitch radius 10.5 mm) drives both fingers in opposite directions on two 8 mm rods: pads stay parallel by construction

checks.name: grip:finger_stress
checks.detail: stall force 140 N at 54 mm gives 12.1 MPa in the 26 x 12 mm finger root vs 20 MPa allowable (PETG across layers)

checks.name: grip:bushing_load
checks.detail: pitch moment of the stall force over the 36 mm rod spacing loads one LM8UU with 364 N vs 392 N static rating

checks.name: grip:hold
checks.detail: rated pinion torque 0.9807 N·m gives 46.7 N per finger; with friction 0.5 two pads hold 4.76 kg vs payload 0.5 kg x 1.5

checks.name: power:supply
checks.detail: servo stall current 2.7 A vs 6 A supply

performance.mount: ISO 9409-1-50-4-M6 style adapter (4 x M6 on PCD 50, 31.5 mm centring recess)
performance.cost_breakdown: parts 68.52 USD, filament 9.79 USD (0.39 kg), fasteners ~3.00 USD

assumptions: Grip force uses the servo's rated (continuous) torque 0.9807 N·m; stall torque 2.942 N·m gives 140 N per finger for short squeezes.
Friction coefficient 0.5 between the printed pads (or TPU/rubber pads glued into the grooves) and the object; safety factor 1.5.

The fingers are coupled by the rack-and-pinion: finger_a is the actuated prismatic joint (servo torque / pitch radius), finger_b and the pinion carry a URDF <mimic> of it (MuJoCo: joint equality constraints), so one actuator drives both fingers.
Rack/pinion teeth are module 1.5 printed in PETG; grease them and expect backlash of a few tenths of a millimetre.
Servo bus adapter and 12 V supply sit off the gripper (cable through the window under the servo).
The adapter plate bolts to the robot first (heads sunk in the plate), then the housing slides over it and is fixed by four radial M4 screws.
